description:
BenchBox wrote duplicate generated benchmark data under worktree-local
`benchmark_runs/` directories even when UAT was invoked with
`BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR=~/Developer/benchmark_runs`.

Observed impact from the 2026-06-01 investigation:

- `/Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox/benchmark_runs` contained about 6.2G of
  generated artifacts, mostly `datagen/`, with large SF1 benchmark data.
- `/Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox.pool-01/benchmark_runs` contained about
  4.2G of similar generated artifacts written on 2026-06-01 while running
  the ClickHouse server corpus from branch `verify/clickhouse-server-corpus`.
- The ClickHouse corpus command did set
  `BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR=~/Developer/benchmark_runs`, so the failure is not
  just missing environment configuration.

The root cause is lifecycle ordering. The CLI orchestrator constructs a
benchmark before the runner resolves the final output root. `BaseBenchmark`
defaults to `Path.cwd() / "benchmark_runs" / "datagen" / ...` when no
`output_dir` is supplied, and several benchmark classes construct nested
`data_generator` instances in `__init__` from that initial path. Later,
`_resolve_output_dir_handler` mutates only `benchmark.output_dir`; nested
generator paths can remain pointed at the worktree-local default. The MCP
benchmark path has the same pattern: it computes data paths after constructing
benchmark instances without an explicit output root.

Correct this at the architecture boundary so explicit CLI `--output` and
`BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR` are resolved before benchmark construction wherever
possible, and ensure any post-construction output-dir mutation updates nested
generators for benchmark families that support generation.

`BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR` remains the shared-root mechanism for UAT and scripted runs.
